done_when: forge land and forge close never stop just because checks are queued: land keeps waiting, and close's wait line says plainly that the checks are queued, for how long, and that the shared runners may be busy or no runner may match the runner setting; only forge doctor reports a likely missing runner, and only when no job of this repo needing that runner has run in the last several days; the no-runner advice no longer tells people to run forge sync unless they changed the runner setting; command tests with a faked GitHub cover a long busy queue that then passes and a repo whose runner never picks anything up, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: Raise: Functional. Doctor still diagnoses a missing runner from demand that a successful retry already resolved. An unassigned attempt that expired ten days ago sets both demand flags here, even if its retry succeeded eight days ago and all current checks are green. The successful retry falls outside the activity window and never clears those flags. src/forge/doctor.py:380–385 calls this for open pull requests without requiring pending checks. Resolved history can also supply old_demand for a fresh, short queue, incorrectly treating it as seven days of unmet demand. The previously reported gap remains open: exclude resolved attempts while retaining expired demand whose retries remain unmet.
findings.title: Ignore resolved attempts when detecting current runner demand

findings.body: Raise: Scale. When no recent matching activity exists, doctor now requests jobs serially for every retained workflow run, including old completed workflows using unrelated runners. There is no history cutoff or demand-based guard. Switching a documented runner setting in a repository with 5,000 retained runs therefore requires at least 5,000 job requests plus workflow-list pagination on every doctor invocation, even for a short queue. This creates thousands of network round trips and exceeds a standard authenticated user's hourly request budget if completed within that hour. The previous implementation skipped completed runs predating the queue. Restrict activity lookups to the relevant window and older demand lookups to unresolved candidates. [GitHub rate limits](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api).
findings.title: Bound doctor's job-history requests

why: v1.2.8's 'checks stayed queued for five minutes; no runner has picked them up' stop still fires when the organisation's shared runner pool is only busy (a client's checks queued behind other repos' runs, 2026-10-09), and its advice to run forge sync can't help; one repo can't tell a busy shared pool from a missing runner within five minutes
